questions.questionText: What was Afrikaner nationalism?

options.text: Political identity emphasizing Afrikaner culture and language

questions.explanation: Afrikaner nationalism promoted Dutch/Afrikaans language, Calvinist religion, and political solidarity among white Afrikaans speakers.

questions.questionText: Who founded the African National Congress (ANC)?
questions.explanation: John Dube was elected first president of the ANC at its founding in 1912.

questions.questionText: What was the purpose of the Orange Free State?

options.text: Independent Afrikaner republic during apartheid era

questions.explanation: The Orange Free State was an independent Boer Republic that became a province in the Union of South Africa.

questions.questionText: What did the Freedom Charter (1955) demand?

options.text: Democratic rights and资源共享 for all South Africans

questions.explanation: The Freedom Charter declared that South Africa belonged to all who lived in it, demanding equality and democratic rights.

questions.questionText: What was the Broederbond?
questions.explanation: The Broederbond was a secretive Afrikaner organization that influenced politics, education, and apartheid policies.

questions.questionText: Who was J.B.M. Hertzog?

options.text: National Party founder promoting Afrikaner interests

questions.explanation: Hertzog co-founded the National Party in 1914 and served as Prime Minister from 1924-1939.

questions.questionText: What role did language play in Afrikaner nationalism?

options.text: Central to cultural identity and political mobilization

questions.explanation: Afrikaans language became central to Afrikaner identity, promoted through education, churches, and cultural institutions.

questions.questionText: How did African nationalism develop in South Africa?

options.text: Through resistance to discriminatory laws and demand for rights
As a copy of European nationalism

questions.explanation: African nationalism emerged as response to colonial rule, pass laws, and land dispossession.

questions.questionText: What was the role of the Dutch Reformed Church in nationalism?

options.text: Provided religious justification for Afrikaner identity and apartheid

questions.explanation: Dutch Reformed Church provided theological legitimacy for Afrikaner nationalism and apartheid policies.

questions.questionText: What was theunis de Kock's contribution?
questions.explanation: De Kock promoted Afrikaner culture, language, and economic empowerment through institutions and media.

questions.questionText: How did the Great Trek shape Afrikaner nationalism?

options.text: Created myth of suffering and chosen people

questions.explanation: The Great Trek became central to Afrikaner identity, portrayed as divine deliverance from British oppression.

questions.questionText: What was the difference between African and Afrikaner nationalism?

options.text: African nationalism sought rights for black majority, Afrikaner for white group

questions.explanation: African nationalism fought for majority rights while Afrikaner nationalism protected minority privileges.

questions.questionText: What was the torch of the Afrikaner people?
questions.explanation: The 'volksmoeder' (mother of the nation) ideal promoted Afrikaner women's role in preserving culture.

questions.questionText: How did the National Party use nationalism to win power?

options.text: Promised to protect Afrikaner privileges and promote their interests
Advocated for all South Africans equally
Made no promises about Afrikaner interests

questions.explanation: National Party won 1948 by appealing to Afrikaner fears and promising to protect white privileges through apartheid.

questions.questionText: Analyze the relationship between Afrikaner nationalism and apartheid.

options.text: Nationalism provided ideological foundation for apartheid policies

questions.explanation: Afrikaner nationalism's emphasis on ethnic purity and separate development provided framework for apartheid.

questions.questionText: Evaluate the role of culture in sustaining nationalism.

options.text: Language, religion, and history created collective identity and loyalty
Culture had no role in nationalism

questions.explanation: Cultural institutions like churches, schools, and language academies reinforced Afrikaner collective identity.

questions.questionText: To what extent was South African nationalism inclusive or exclusive?

options.text: Exclusionary, defining nation by race and excluding the majority

questions.explanation: Both Afrikaner and African nationalism were shaped by racial identities, though with opposing constituencies.

questions.questionText: Analyze the impact of nationalism on South African politics.

options.text: Created deep racial divisions and shaped all political outcomes

questions.explanation: Nationalist politics polarized South Africa along racial lines for much of the 20th century.

questions.questionText: How did the memories of the Boer War influence Afrikaner politics?

options.text: Created lasting resentment and desire for self-determination

questions.explanation: Boer War trauma, especially concentration camp deaths, fueled Afrikaner political mobilization and eventual National Party victory.

questions.questionText: Evaluate the legacy of nationalist movements for post-apartheid South Africa.

options.text: Created lasting divisions but also framework for reconciliation

questions.explanation: Nationalist legacies continue to shape identity politics while Truth and Reconciliation attempted to bridge divides.
